mainTopic: The source for רבי יוחנן's view on בכורות in the מדבר, and קונטרוקוס's questions about the לויים and the משכן silver
overview: This amud finishes the מחלוקת between רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש about whether בכורות were holy in the מדבר. רבי אלעזר brings רבי יוחנן's source, ״לִי יִהְיוּ״, and the גמרא explains how רבי יוחנן reads ריש לקיש's פסוק: do this מצוה, and in its merit you will enter the land. רב מרדכי reports a version with the opinions flipped. He explains that the wording means the same thing and that he keeps it because one must speak בלשון רבו. Next, קונטרוקוס challenges רבן יוחנן בן זכאי about the numbers in the Torah. The missing 300 לויים were בכורות themselves, and אביי explains that a לוי בכור only frees his own holiness. קונטרוקוס then accuses משה of losing half the silver of the משכן. רבן יוחנן בן זכאי answers that the holy מנה was double. The גמרא searches for the source of that claim. Two proofs, from the hooks and from the copper, are pushed aside, and the amud ends as רב חסדא brings a verse from יחזקאל that defines the מנה.

steps.title: End of ריש לקיש's position: the holiness stopped
steps.stepSummary: The closing word of ריש לקיש's final position: the בכורות were holy, and then their holiness stopped.
steps.simpleTranslation: And then their holiness stopped.
steps.whatsHappening: This single word finishes ריש לקיש's statement from the previous lines. In his view, the firstborns were holy at first, but that holiness stopped after the census in the מדבר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ריש לקיש agrees the בכורות were once holy (from יציאת מצרים). His claim is that this holiness ended and only started again once the Jews entered ארץ ישראל. This is the position the next step is built on.

keyTerms.meaning: They stopped / ceased (the holiness came to an end)
The אמורא who argues with רבי יוחנן here

steps.confusionAlert: This word is not a new statement. It is the very end of ריש לקיש's sentence on the previous amud (roughly: 'they became holy, and then stopped').

phrases.english: and [then their holiness] ceased.
phrases.notes: Tail end of ריש לקיש's statement from the previous lines.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּפָסְקוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes ריש לקיש's position from the preceding text.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to ריש לקיש, the בכורות were holy and then their holiness ceased in the מדבר.

steps.title: ריש לקיש has a source, but what is רבי יוחנן's?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא grants that ריש לקיש has a clear reason and asks what רבי יוחנן's source is.
steps.simpleTranslation: It makes sense for ריש לקיש, whose reason is what he said. But for רבי יוחנן, what is his reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא accepts that ריש לקיש has a פסוק and asks for רבי יוחנן's source. This step sets up the next move, where an answer is given.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ריש לקיש's reason is the פסוק ״וְהָיָה כִּי יְבִיאֲךָ״, which ties the מצוה of בכורות to coming into the land. רבי יוחנן says the holiness continued in the מדבר, so he needs a פסוק that shows the holiness never stopped.

keyTerms.meaning: It makes sense / granted (for one side)
But (for the other side, there is a problem)

phrases.english: Granted, according to Reish Lakish,
the reason is as he said,
phrases.notes: Refers to the פסוק ״והיה כי יביאך״.

phrases.english: but according to Rabbi Yochanan, what is the reason?

steps.triggerLanguage: בִּשְׁלָמָא רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ, כִּדְאָמַר טַעַם, אֶלָּא לְרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן מַאי טַעְמָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: With ריש לקיש's view settled, the גמרא turns to find רבי יוחנן's source.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which פסוק supports רבי יוחנן's view that the בכורות stayed holy in the מדבר?

steps.title: רבי אלעזר's dream and the verse 'Mine they shall be'
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר brings ״לִי יִהְיוּ״, meaning the בכורות stay in their holy state. He adds that seeing רבי יוחנן in a dream shows his explanation is correct.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר said: I saw רבי יוחנן in a dream, which shows I am saying something good. The פסוק says 'Mine they shall be': they shall stay as they are.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אלעזר gives רבי יוחנן's source: the words ״לִי יִהְיוּ״. He reads them as 'they will remain in their state,' meaning holy.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word ״יִהְיוּ״ ('they shall be') is read as a lasting state: once holy, the בכורות stay holy. So their holiness did not stop in the מדבר. The dream about his teacher is a sign to רבי אלעזר that he explained רבי יוחנן correctly.
steps.whyThisMatters: This gives רבי יוחנן a solid source from the פסוק, so both sides of the מחלוקת now rest on a verse.

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar said:
I saw Rabbi Yochanan in a dream,
which shows I am saying a fine matter;
the verse says: 'Mine they shall be':
they shall remain in their [holy] state.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question about רבי יוחנן's source.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: ״לִי יִהְיוּ״ teaches that the בכורות remain in their holy state, so the holiness never stopped.

steps.title: What does רבי יוחנן do with ריש לקיש's verse?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how רבי יוחנן uses the פסוק ״וְהָיָה כִּי יְבִיאֲךָ... וְהַעֲבַרְתָּ״, which ריש לקיש relied on.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יוחנן, what does he do with 'And it shall be when He brings you... and you shall set apart'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what רבי יוחנן learns from the פסוק ריש לקיש used. This sets up the next step's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: That פסוק seems to say the מצוה of בכורות starts only in ארץ ישראל, which fits ריש לקיש. If רבי יוחנן does not read it that way, the פסוק must teach something else, since a פסוק is not left without a lesson.

keyTerms.meaning: What does he do with it? (How does he use this פסוק?)
And you shall set apart (the firstborn)

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yochanan, 'And it shall be when He brings you... and you shall set apart':
what does he do with it?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן, וְהָיָה כִּי יְבִיאֲךָ וְהַעֲבַרְתָּ, מַאי עָבֵיד לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Now that רבי יוחנן has his own source, the גמרא asks how he handles the other side's פסוק.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What lesson does רבי יוחנן learn from ״וְהָיָה כִּי יְבִיאֲךָ״?

steps.title: The verse teaches: do this מצוה to merit entering the land
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן uses the פסוק for the teaching of the תנא דבי רבי ישמעאל: perform this מצוה, and in its merit you will enter ארץ ישראל.
steps.simpleTranslation: He needs that פסוק for what the school of רבי ישמעאל taught: do this מצוה, because in its merit you will enter the land.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that רבי יוחנן reads the פסוק as a reward: keeping the מצוה of בכורות earns entry into the land. It does not mean the מצוה only starts there.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both sides agree the פסוק links בכורות to the land. They disagree about how. For ריש לקיש, the land is when the מצוה begins. For רבי יוחנן, the מצוה is the cause and entering the land is the reward.

keyTerms.meaning: He needs it (for a different teaching)
A תנא of the school of רבי ישמעאל taught
In its merit / because of it

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יוחנן: the בכורות stayed holy in the מדבר (״לִי יִהְיוּ״), and ״וְהָיָה כִּי יְבִיאֲךָ״ teaches that this מצוה earns entry into the land. ריש לקיש: the holiness ceased in the מדבר and resumed in the land.
steps.confusionAlert: ״כִּי יְבִיאֲךָ״ sounds like a time limit ('when you enter'). For רבי יוחנן it is a reward ('in its merit you will enter'), not a starting point for the מצוה.

phrases.english: That [verse] is needed by him
for that which the tanna of the school of Rabbi Yishmael taught:
Perform this מצוה,
for in its merit you will enter the land.

steps.triggerLanguage: הַהוּא מִיבְּעֵי לֵיהּ לְכִדְתָנָא דְּבֵי רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of how רבי יוחנן uses ריש לקיש's פסוק.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reassigning the פסוק to a different teaching (מיבעי ליה)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The פסוק seemed to show that the מצוה of בכורות begins only in ארץ ישראל, which would contradict רבי יוחנן.
steps.terutzMaskana: For רבי יוחנן, the פסוק teaches that keeping this מצוה earns entry into the land, so it does not limit when the מצוה applies.

steps.title: רב מרדכי's reversed version of the dispute
steps.stepSummary: רב מרדכי tells רב אשי that in his tradition the names are flipped: רבי יוחנן says the בכורות were not sanctified in the מדבר, and ריש לקיש says they were.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב מרדכי said to רב אשי: You teach it this way. We teach it the opposite way. רבי יוחנן says the firstborn were not made holy in the desert, and ריש לקיש says the firstborn were made holy in the desert.
steps.whatsHappening: A new חכם reports a different tradition of the same מחלוקת, with the two opinions switched between רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Until now, רבי יוחנן held the בכורות stayed holy (from 'לי יהיו') and ריש לקיש held their holiness stopped. רב מרדכי's wording seems to give each one the other's position. This sets up the next question: does the whole סוגיא then have to be flipped too?

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב מָרְדֳּכַי לְרַב אָשֵׁי:
phrases.english: Rav Mordechai said to Rav Ashi:
You teach it this way,
we teach it the opposite way:

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן אָמַר: לֹא קָדְשׁוּ בְּכוֹרוֹת בַּמִּדְבָּר,
phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan says: the firstborn were not sanctified in the desert,

phrases.aramaic: וְרֵישׁ לָקִישׁ אָמַר: קָדְשׁוּ בְּכוֹרוֹת בַּמִּדְבָּר.
phrases.english: and Reish Lakish says: the firstborn were sanctified in the desert.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַתּוּן הָכִי מַתְנִיתוּ לַהּ, אֲנַן אִיפְּכָא מַתְנִינַן לַהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a competing tradition of the מחלוקת whose sources were just analyzed.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In רב מרדכי's tradition, רבי יוחנן says 'לא קדשו בכורות במדבר' and ריש לקיש says 'קדשו בכורות במדבר'.

steps.title: Do you flip the proofs and the dream too?
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי challenges רב מרדכי: if you flip the names, you must also flip the objections and רבי אלעזר's dream statement. That does not seem to work.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said to him: Do you also flip the objection? And do you also flip what רבי אלעזר said?
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי pushes back on the reversed version. He points out that the rest of the סוגיא is built around the original assignment of opinions.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proofs, the objections, and רבי אלעזר's dream (in which רבי יוחנן's view was confirmed) all assume רבי יוחנן held the בכורות stayed holy. Flipping only the names would leave the whole סוגיא mismatched. So רב אשי is asking whether רב מרדכי really means to rewrite everything.

phrases.english: He said to him: And do you also reverse the objection,
and do you reverse that statement of Rabbi Elazar?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָפְכִית נָמֵי תְּיוּבָתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the reversed version presented in step 6.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב מרדכי's reversed version of the מחלוקת
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Flipping the names would also require flipping the proofs and רבי אלעזר's dream, and the סוגיא does not fit that.

steps.title: 'Not sanctified' means 'did not need sanctifying'
steps.stepSummary: רב מרדכי explains that 'לא קדשו' in his version means the בכורות did not need to be made holy, because they were already holy.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: When I say 'they were not sanctified,' I mean they did not need to be sanctified, because they were already holy.
steps.whatsHappening: רב מרדכי answers רב אשי. He shows that his wording means the same thing as רב אשי's version.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In his version, רבי יוחנן's 'לא קדשו' means no one had to declare the בכורות holy. They were holy on their own, which is exactly רבי יוחנן's view in רב אשי's version. So nothing needs to be flipped except the surface words.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't read 'לא קדשו' as 'they were not holy.' In רב מרדכי's version it means the opposite: they were so holy that they needed no act of sanctifying.

phrases.english: He said to him: 'They were not sanctified' means —
they did not need to be sanctified.

steps.triggerLanguage: לֹא קָדְשׁוּ לְהוּ — לֹא הוּצְרְכוּ לִיקְדַּשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב אשי's challenge from step 7.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The reversed version flips the actual opinions, so the whole סוגיא would have to be flipped.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only the words differ. 'לא קדשו' means the בכורות were already holy and needed no act of sanctifying.

steps.title: Then it is the same as our version
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: if so, רב מרדכי's version is identical in meaning to רב אשי's. Why report it at all?
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, that is the same as our version!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the point of the whole exchange. If the meaning is the same, what did רב מרדכי add?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 8 showed the two versions agree in substance. Now the problem is the opposite one: there seems to be no reason to mention the alternate version.

keyTerms.meaning: That is the same as ours

phrases.english: If so, that is the same as ours!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי הָכִי, הַיְינוּ דִּידַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns the answer of step 8 into a new challenge: the reported version adds nothing.
steps.kashyaTarget: The purpose of רב מרדכי's alternate version
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If both versions mean the same thing, reporting the alternate wording seems pointless.

steps.title: One must use his teacher's exact words
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the lesson is that a person must repeat a teaching in his teacher's own wording.
steps.simpleTranslation: It teaches us that a person must say a teaching in the words of his teacher.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why רב מרדכי kept his teacher's wording even though the meaning was the same.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב מרדכי did not change 'לא קדשו' into clearer words, even though it was confusing. He held on to the exact language he received. That faithfulness to the teacher's words is itself the lesson.
steps.whatToRemember: The two versions of the רבי יוחנן–ריש לקיש מחלוקת agree in meaning. רב מרדכי kept his version's wording because 'חייב אדם לומר בלשון רבו'.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is a well-known principle of passing on Torah: we keep the exact words we received, not just their meaning.

phrases.english: It teaches us:
a person must say it in the language of his teacher.

steps.triggerLanguage: קָא מַשְׁמַע לַן: חַיָּיב אָדָם לוֹמַר בִּלְשׁוֹן רַבּוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 9.
steps.terutzMaskana: It teaches that a teaching must be passed on in the teacher's exact words.

steps.title: קונטרוקוס asks about the missing 300 לויים
steps.stepSummary: קונטרוקוס the officer asks רבן יוחנן בן זכאי: the family counts of the לויים add up to 22,300, but the total says 22,000. Where did the other 300 go?
steps.simpleTranslation: קונטרוקוס the officer asked רבן יוחנן בן זכאי: When you add up the separate counts of the לויים, you get 22,300. But the total count says 22,000. Where did the 300 go?
steps.whatsHappening: A new section opens with a question about the numbers in the פסוקים. This sets up an explanation connected to the לויים replacing the בכורות in the מדבר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each family of לוי is counted separately in the פסוקים, and those numbers add up to 22,300. Yet the פסוק gives the total as 22,000. That 22,000 total is what was matched against the בכורות, so the gap needs an explanation.

phrases.aramaic: שָׁאַל קוּנְטְרוּקוּס הַשַּׂר אֶת רַבָּן יוֹחָנָן בֶּן זַכַּאי:
phrases.english: Kontrokos the officer asked Rabban Yochanan ben Zakkai:
In the individual counts of the Levites you find
twenty-two thousand three hundred,

phrases.aramaic: בִּכְלָלָן אַתָּה מוֹצֵא עֶשְׂרִים וּשְׁנַיִם אֶלֶף,
phrases.english: but in their total you find twenty-two thousand;
where did the three hundred go?

steps.triggerLanguage: שָׁאַל קוּנְטְרוּקוּס הַשַּׂר אֶת רַבָּן יוֹחָנָן בֶּן זַכַּאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins a new section about the count of the לויים who replaced the בכורות.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why the family counts of the לויים total 22,300 while the פסוק's total is 22,000.

steps.title: The extra 300 לויים were firstborns themselves
steps.stepSummary: רבן יוחנן בן זכאי explains that 300 of the לויים were בכורות, and a בכור cannot redeem another בכור. So they were left out of the total.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Those three hundred were firstborns, and a firstborn cannot cancel the holiness of another firstborn.
steps.whatsHappening: רבן יוחנן בן זכאי answers the question from Step 11. The Torah's total of 22,000 counts only the לויים who could redeem a ישראל בכור, and 300 לויים could not.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each לוי took the place of one ישראל בכור. 300 of the לויים were firstborns themselves, so they could not take another firstborn's place. That is why the Torah's total is 22,000 and not 22,300.

keyTerms.meaning: A firstborn. Firstborns had special holiness after מצרים.
Cancels / removes (here: removes the holiness of a firstborn by taking his place)

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר לוֹ: אוֹתָן שְׁלֹשׁ מֵאוֹת בְּכוֹרוֹת הָיוּ,
phrases.english: He said to him: Those three hundred were firstborns,
phrases.notes: רבן יוחנן בן זכאי is answering קונטרוקוס.

phrases.english: and a firstborn cannot cancel the holiness of a firstborn.
phrases.notes: A לוי בכור cannot replace a ישראל בכור.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לוֹ: אוֹתָן שְׁלֹשׁ מֵאוֹת בְּכוֹרוֹת הָיוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Directly answers the question about the missing 300 לויים.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The 300 were בכורות, and a בכור cannot redeem another בכור. So only 22,000 counted toward the redemption.

steps.title: Why can't a firstborn redeem a firstborn?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the reason behind the rule that a בכור cannot redeem another בכור.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא stops to ask why the rule from Step 12 is true. This sets up אביי's explanation in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 12 gave a rule without a reason. A לוי בכור is still a לוי, so one could ask why he cannot replace a ישראל בכור. The גמרא wants the logic.

phrases.english: What is the reason?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי טַעְמָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reason behind the rule in Step 12.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The logic behind 'a בכור cannot redeem a בכור.'

steps.title: A firstborn's power only covers himself
steps.stepSummary: אביי explains that a לוי בכור's ability to cancel holiness is used up on his own firstborn status.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: It is enough for a firstborn to cancel his own holiness.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי answers the question from Step 13. A לוי who is a בכור uses his לוי status to cancel his own firstborn holiness, so nothing is left over to cover someone else.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Being a לוי can replace one firstborn's holiness. A לוי בכור has his own firstborn holiness to deal with first. His לוי status is spent on himself, so he cannot also free a ישראל בכור.
steps.whatToRemember: The 300 missing לויים were בכורות. Their לוי status only freed themselves, so they could not redeem ישראל בכורות. That is why the total is 22,000.

phrases.english: Abaye said:
It is enough for a firstborn to cancel his own holiness.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי: דַּיּוֹ לַבְּכוֹר שֶׁיַּפְקִיעַ קְדוּשַּׁת עַצְמוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the 'why' question from Step 13.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A לוי בכור's power to cancel holiness covers only his own firstborn status.

steps.title: The amount of silver collected for the משכן
steps.stepSummary: קונטרוקוס starts a new question. Based on the half-shekel per person, the silver collected comes to 201 ככר and 11 מנה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And he asked him more: In the collection of silver you find 201 ככר and 11 מנה, as it is written: 'A בקע a head, half a שקל by the שקל הקודש...'
steps.whatsHappening: קונטרוקוס opens a second question by stating the first number: how much silver was collected. This sets up the contradiction in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 603,550 men each gave half a shekel, which equals 301,775 shekels. Using 25 shekels per מנה and 60 מנה per ככר, that comes to 201 ככר and 11 מנה. Step 16 will compare this with the amount the Torah says was used.

keyTerms.meaning: A talent, a large unit of weight or money
A maneh, a smaller unit (25 regular shekels)
The holy shekel, the shekel used for the מקדש

phrases.english: And he asked him more:
In the collection of silver you find

phrases.aramaic: מָאתַיִם וְאַחַת כִּכָּר וְאַחַת עֶשְׂרֵה מָנֶה,
phrases.english: two hundred and one talents and eleven maneh,
as it is written: 'A beka a head,'
'half a shekel by the holy shekel, etc.'

steps.triggerLanguage: וְעוֹד שְׁאָלוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a brand-new question from קונטרוקוס about the משכן silver.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Sets up the first number (silver collected) for a contradiction.

steps.title: Only 100 talents used, so was משה dishonest?
steps.stepSummary: The Torah says only 100 ככר were used. קונטרוקוס accuses משה of stealing, gambling, or bad arithmetic.
steps.simpleTranslation: But in the giving of the silver you find 100 ככר, as it is written: 'And the hundred ככר of silver were for casting...' Was משה רבכם a thief, or a gambler, or not good at math? He gave half and took half, and he did not even return a full half!
steps.whatsHappening: קונטרוקוס points out that the Torah's spending total, 100 ככר, is less than half of what was collected. He uses this to attack משה רבינו's honesty or skill.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 201 ככר and 11 מנה came in, but only 100 ככר were used for the sockets. That is less than even half. קונטרוקוס offers three explanations: theft, gambling the money away, or a counting mistake.

keyTerms.meaning: The giving (using) of the silver for the משכן

steps.confusionAlert: Note that קונטרוקוס says 'משה רבכם', 'your teacher'. He is an outsider mocking משה. When רבן יוחנן בן זכאי answers, he says 'משה רבינו', 'our teacher'.

phrases.aramaic: וּבִנְתִינַת הַכֶּסֶף אַתָּה מוֹצֵא מְאַת כִּכָּר,
phrases.english: But in the giving of the silver you find one hundred talents,

phrases.aramaic: דִּכְתִיב: ״וַיְהִי מְאַת כִּכַּר הַכֶּסֶף לָצֶקֶת וְגוֹ׳״.
phrases.english: as it is written: 'And the hundred talents of silver were for casting, etc.'
Was Moses your teacher a thief,
or was he a gambler,
or was he not good at accounting?
He gave half and took half,
and he did not even give back a full half.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּבִנְתִינַת הַכֶּסֶף אַתָּה מוֹצֵא מְאַת כִּכָּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the second number and turns the gap into an accusation.
steps.kashyaTarget: The Torah's numbers for the משכן silver, and משה רבינו's honesty.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: 201 ככר were collected but only 100 were used, so about half seems missing.

steps.title: The holy מנה was double, so the numbers match
steps.stepSummary: רבן יוחנן בן זכאי answers that משה was honest and good at math. The 100 ככר were measured with a holy מנה worth double, so they equal the 200+ collected.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: משה רבינו was a trustworthy treasurer, and he was expert in accounting, and the מנה של קודש was double.
steps.whatsHappening: רבן יוחנן בן זכאי defends משה and solves the math. The 100 ככר were counted in holy units, which are twice as large.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A regular מנה is 25 shekels, but a מנה של קודש is 50. So 100 holy ככר are worth 200 regular ככר. That matches the amount collected, and nothing was missing.

keyTerms.meaning: A holy maneh, the unit used for the מקדש

steps.whatToRemember: The silver numbers in the Torah do not conflict. The 100 ככר were measured in holy units, worth double, so they match the 200+ ככר collected.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר לוֹ: מֹשֶׁה רַבֵּינוּ גִּיזְבָּר נֶאֱמָן הָיָה,
phrases.english: He said to him: Moses our teacher was a trustworthy treasurer,
and he was expert in accounting,
and the maneh of the Sanctuary was double.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לוֹ: מֹשֶׁה רַבֵּינוּ גִּיזְבָּר נֶאֱמָן הָיָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the accusation in Step 16.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefines the unit of measure: the two verses use different-sized units.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both numbers use the same ככר, so half the silver is missing.
steps.terutzMaskana: The 100 ככר were in holy units worth double, so they equal the amount collected.

steps.title: Why was the 100 ככר verse even a problem?
steps.stepSummary: רב אחאי asks what made קונטרוקוס's question so strong. The verse about 100 ככר speaks only of silver used for casting the sockets, so the other 100 ככר could have gone to the treasury.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אחאי discussed it: What was so difficult? Was it the verse "And the hundred ככר of silver were for casting"? Those 100 were for casting, and the other 100 went to the treasury!
steps.whatsHappening: רב אחאי goes back and tests the original question of קונטרוקוס. He suggests the question may not have been a real problem at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: קונטרוקוס said only 100 ככר were used, while more than 200 were collected. But the verse he quoted only says 100 ככר went to casting the sockets. So the remaining silver could simply have been stored in the treasury, and nobody stole anything.

phrases.english: Rav Achai discussed it:
What was difficult for him?
Was it "And the hundred talents of silver were for casting, etc."?
phrases.notes: שמות 38:27, about the sockets of the משכן

phrases.english: These were for casting,
and those others were in the treasury!

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי קָא קַשְׁיָא לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to test whether קונטרוקוס's question was valid in the first place
steps.kashyaTarget: The basis of קונטרוקוס's question in Step 16
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The verse only describes the silver used for casting, not the total collected. The extra silver could have been stored.

steps.title: A second verse gives the total as 100 ככר
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that a different verse describes the total silver counted from the people, and it also says 100 ככר.
steps.simpleTranslation: Another verse is written: "And the silver of those counted of the congregation was a hundred ככר."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends קונטרוקוס's question by pointing to another verse about the total amount collected.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמות 38:25 describes all the silver collected from the people, not just the part used for casting. It says 100 ככר. So the 'treasury' answer does not work, and the gap between 100 and 201 is a real question.

keyTerms.meaning: Those who were counted in the congregation

phrases.english: Another verse is written:
"And the silver of those counted of the congregation was a hundred talents, etc."

steps.triggerLanguage: כְּתַב קְרָא אַחֲרִינָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב אחאי's challenge and confirms the original question was real
steps.terutzResolutionType: Citing a second verse that covers the total amount
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The 100 ככר was only the casting portion, and the rest was stored
steps.terutzMaskana: The total collected is also given as 100 ככר, so the difficulty stands and needs רבן יוחנן בן זכאי's answer
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows why רבן יוחנן בן זכאי needed the 'double מנה' answer. A simple 'it was stored' answer would not work.

steps.title: How did he know the holy מנה was double?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the source of רבן יוחנן בן זכאי's claim that a מנה של קודש was worth twice a regular מנה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And what he told him, that the holy מנה was double, where does he know that from?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now asks for the source behind רבן יוחנן בן זכאי's answer. This sets up the proof in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: His whole answer depends on the holy מנה being worth double. The גמרא wants a source in the verses, so the answer is not just an invention to escape the question.

keyTerms.meaning: The holy (Sanctuary) מנה, a unit of weight
From where does he know it?

phrases.english: And that which he said to him:
"The holy maneh was double"
from where does he know this?

steps.triggerLanguage: וּדְקָאָמַר לֵיהּ מָנֶה שֶׁל קוֹדֶשׁ כָּפוּל הָיָה מְנָא לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of the claim used in Step 17's answer
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The scriptural source showing that a מנה של קודש was worth double

steps.title: Proof from the 1,775 שקלים for the hooks
steps.stepSummary: The Torah lists 1,775 שקלים for the hooks. With a regular מנה, that equals 71 מנה, which is one ככר and 11 מנה. The verse would then have written the total as 101 ככר and 11 מנה, but it did not.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say the source is the verse itself: here are 71 מנה, "and from the 1,775 he made hooks for the pillars." Yet the verse counted them only in small coins. If a regular מנה were meant, the verse should have said 101 ככר and 11 מנה!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the proof from the same passage. It points to the way the Torah counts the silver for the hooks.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A regular מנה is 25 שקלים, so 1,775 שקלים equals 71 מנה. A ככר is 60 מנה, so 71 מנה would be more than a full ככר, and the Torah should have added it to the 100 ככר. Since the Torah kept it in small coins, it must have been less than one ככר.
steps.confusionAlert: As usual, אילימא introduces a suggestion that the גמרא will reject. Step 22 finishes this proof, and Step 23 (ודילמא) knocks it down. Then Step 24 (אלא מהכא) brings a different verse.

phrases.english: If you say it is from the verse itself,
for here there are seventy-one maneh:
"And of the one thousand seven hundred seventy-five
he made hooks for the pillars"
and the verse counted them only in small units,
and if it were so (that a regular maneh is meant),

phrases.aramaic: מֵאָה וְאֶחָד כִּכָּר וְאַחַת עֶשְׂרֵה מָנֶה מִיבְּעֵי לֵיהּ!
phrases.english: it should have said one hundred and one talents and eleven maneh!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִילֵימָא מִינֵּיהּ שֶׁהֲרֵי כָּאן שִׁבְעִים וְאֶחָד מָנֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 20's question by bringing a proof from the verses
steps.raayaObject: That a מנה של קודש was worth double a regular מנה
steps.raayaSupportSource: שמות 38:28, where 1,775 שקלים are listed in small units and not added to the ככר total

steps.title: The hooks proof: the holy מנה was double
steps.stepSummary: Since the Torah left the 1,775 שקלים in small units, the גמרא concludes that a holy מנה was double. That makes the amount only 35½ holy מנה, less than one ככר.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, since the verse counted them only in small units, learn from it: the holy מנה was double.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the proof from the hooks: since the verse left the שקלים in small units, the holy מנה must have been double. The very next step rejects this proof.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With a holy מנה of 50 שקלים, 1,775 שקלים equals only 35½ מנה. That is less than a ככר of 60 מנה, so it makes sense to list it in small units. The proof depends on assuming the Torah would always convert a full ככר into ככרים, and Step 23 challenges that assumption.

phrases.english: Rather, since the verse did not count them
except in small units,
learn from it:
the holy maneh was double.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא מִדְּלֹא מְנָאָן הַכָּתוּב אֶלָּא בִּפְרוֹטְרוֹט שְׁמַע מִינַּהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the suggested proof begun in Step 21; Step 23 then rejects it
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the first of three attempts to find a source for the double מנה. Its weakness, that the Torah may not convert every amount into ככרים, drives the next steps.

steps.title: Maybe the Torah only counts big totals in talents
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the proof from the 1,775 שקלים. The Torah may write the large general total in ככרים and leave the smaller leftover amount in שקלים, even if that leftover adds up to a full ככר.
steps.simpleTranslation: But maybe the Torah counts the general amounts (the big totals) in ככרים, and does not count the details (the smaller leftovers) in ככרים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the proof it just gave. Leaving the 1,775 שקלים in small units may not prove anything about the size of a מנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof assumed that if the שקלים added up to a ככר, the Torah would have converted them. The גמרא suggests another possibility. The Torah may write the main total (100 ככר) in ככרים and simply list the leftover in שקלים as a separate detail. If so, a regular-sized מנה still fits the verse.

keyTerms.meaning: But maybe (introduces a possibility that weakens a proof)
ככרים, talents (a large unit of weight)

steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא is not saying the 1,775 שקלים are less than a ככר. It is saying that even if they equal more than a ככר, the Torah might still leave them in שקלים.

phrases.english: But perhaps it counts the general amounts in talents,
but does not count the details in talents!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְדִילְמָא כְּלָלֵי קָחָשֵׁיב בְּכַכְּרֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof from the 1,775 שקלים given in steps 21-22
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The proof from the hooks' 1,775 שקלים
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof assumed the Torah always converts amounts into ככרים. The Torah may only do that for the main total, not for leftover details.

steps.title: New proof from the copper of the offering
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a new proof from the copper: 70 ככר and 2,400 שקלים. With a regular מנה, 2,400 שקלים is 96 מנה, which is more than a ככר. Yet the verse still lists them in small units, so the holy מנה must have been double.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, learn it from here: "And the copper of the offering was 70 ככר and 2,400 שקל." Using a regular מנה, there are 96 מנה here, yet the verse lists them only in small units. Learn from this that a מנה של קודש was double.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new verse, about the copper, to prove the holy מנה was double.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the main number is 70, not a large round total like 100, so the verse does write smaller amounts in ככרים. A regular מנה is 25 שקלים, so 2,400 שקלים would be 96 מנה, which is one ככר (60 מנה) plus 36 more. The verse should then have said 71 ככר, but it did not. If the holy מנה was double (50 שקלים), 2,400 שקלים is only 48 holy מנה, less than a ככר, which explains why the verse kept them in שקלים.

keyTerms.meaning: The copper that was donated as an offering for the משכן
In small units, piece by piece

steps.whyThisMatters: This proof answers the previous rejection. The 70 ככר shows that the Torah does write non-round amounts in ככרים, so the 'only big totals' excuse no longer works.

phrases.english: Rather, from here:
"And the copper of the offering was seventy talents
and two thousand four hundred shekels"
for here there are ninety-six maneh,
phrases.notes: 2,400 ÷ 25 = 96 regular מנה, which is more than one ככר (60 מנה)

phrases.english: and the verse counted them only in small units,
learn from this:
a maneh of the Sanctuary was double.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא מֵהָכָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the rejected proof with a new verse that avoids the 'only big totals' problem
steps.raayaObject: The claim that a מנה של קודש was double a regular מנה
steps.raayaSupportSource: שמות לח:כט: the copper of the offering was 70 ככר and 2,400 שקל

steps.title: Maybe the Torah converts tens of talents but not single talents
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the copper proof too. The Torah may write a large detail (tens of ככרים) in ככרים but not a small detail (one extra ככר).
steps.simpleTranslation: But maybe it counts a big detail in ככרים, and does not count a small detail in ככרים!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the copper proof with a sharper version of the same idea.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Seventy is a large detail, a number in the tens, so the Torah wrote it in ככרים. One extra ככר is a small detail, so the Torah may have left it in שקלים. If so, 2,400 שקלים could be a full regular-sized ככר and more, and the verse still fits a regular מנה.

keyTerms.meaning: A big detail, meaning tens of ככרים
A small detail, meaning single ככרים

phrases.aramaic: וְדִילְמָא פְּרָטָא רַבָּה קָא חָשֵׁיב בְּכַכְּרֵי,
phrases.english: But perhaps it counts a large detail in talents,
but does not count a small detail in talents!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְדִילְמָא פְּרָטָא רַבָּה קָא חָשֵׁיב בְּכַכְּרֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the copper proof from step 24
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The proof from the copper's 2,400 שקלים
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The Torah may convert only tens of ככרים, so one extra ככר could stay in שקלים even with a regular מנה.

steps.title: רב חסדא's proof from the verse in יחזקאל
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא brings a new source from יחזקאל. That verse defines the holy שקל as 20 גרה and the מנה as a sum of 20, 25, and 15 שקלים, which is 60 שקלים.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רב חסדא said: learn it from here: "And the שקל shall be twenty גרה; twenty שקלים, twenty-five שקלים, ten and five שקל shall be your מנה."
steps.whatsHappening: After two proofs from the משכן's metals were rejected, רב חסדא brings a verse that directly defines the size of the holy מנה. The גמרא is setting up a calculation from this verse.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Unlike the earlier proofs, this verse does not depend on guessing how the Torah rounds numbers. It states outright how many שקלים make up the מנה: 20 + 25 + 15 = 60 שקלים. A regular מנה is only 25 שקלים, so this verse shows the holy מנה was larger. The exact calculation is worked out next.

keyTerms.meaning: An אמורא who brings the final source here
A small unit of weight; the holy שקל is 20 of them

steps.whatToRemember: Two proofs from the משכן were rejected because the Torah might round numbers in different ways. רב חסדא avoids that problem with a verse that directly defines the holy מנה in שקלים.

phrases.english: Rather, Rav Ḥisda said: from here,
"And the shekel shall be twenty gera;
twenty shekels, twenty-five shekels,
ten and five shekels,
shall be your maneh."

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא מֵהָכָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the copper proof is rejected, רב חסדא offers a new and more direct source
steps.raayaObject: The claim that a מנה של קודש was larger (double) than a regular מנה
steps.raayaSupportSource: יחזקאל מה:יב, which defines the holy שקל and the מנה in שקלים
